'''Gerasim Matveyevich Eliashberg''' ({{langx|ru|Герасим Матвеевич Элиашберг}}; 26 July 1930 – 8 January 2021) was a Soviet [[theoretical physicist]] best known for developing the [[Eliashberg theory]], a microscopic extension of the [[BCS theory|Bardeen–Cooper–Schrieffer (BCS) theory]] of superconductivity. He also made contributions related to [[Landau's Fermi-liquid theory]], [[nonequilibrium superconductivity]] and other areas of [[condensed matter physics]].

== Biography ==
Eliashberg was born on 26 July 1930 in [[Leningrad]] (now St. Petersburg) to Matvey Gerasimovich Eliashberg and Amalya Yakovlevna. His family, of Jewish origin, had moved from [[Dvinsk]] (present-day Daugavpils, Latvia) to St. Petersburg in 1907. His father was a chemical engineer, and worked as a director in the pulp and paper industry.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Yakov Matveevich Eliashberg |url=https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Eliashberg/ |access-date=2 October 2025 |website=MacTutor |language=en}}</ref><ref name="q351">{{cite journal |date=7 May 2021 |title=Gerasim (Sima) Eliashberg |url=https://pubs.aip.org/physicstoday/online/5672 |journal=Physics Today |volume=2021 |issue=5 |article-number=5672 |doi=10.1063/pt.6.4o.20210507a |bibcode=2021PhT..2021R...4. |access-date=2 October 2025}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Jackson |first=Allyn |date=2024 |title=Interview with Yakov Eliashberg |url=https://celebratio.org/Eliashberg_Y/article/1166/ |access-date=2 October 2025 |website=celebratio.org |language=en}}</ref> As a teenager during the Second World War, Gerasim endured the [[Siege of Leningrad]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Feigel'man |first1=Mikhail |last2=Galitski |first2=Victor |last3=Ivlev |first3=Boris |last4=Levitov |first4=Leonid |last5=Nazarov |first5=Yuli |date=1 June 2020 |title=Foreword to Special Annals of Physics issue, Eliashberg festschrift |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0003491620301226 |journal=Annals of Physics |series=Eliashberg theory at 60: Strong-coupling superconductivity and beyond |volume=417 |article-number=168189 |doi=10.1016/j.aop.2020.168189 |bibcode=2020AnPhy.41768189F |issn=0003-4916|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

In 1947 he enrolled in the Faculty of Physics at [[Leningrad State University]] and graduated with honors in 1952. The growing [[Antisemitism in the Soviet Union|antisemitic persecution in the Soviet Union]] prevented him from working as a scientist, and instead he worked at the ''Krasny Khimik'' ("Red Chemist") chemical plant for the next five years.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /> During this period, he nevertheless managed to publish his first papers on theoretical physics.<ref name=":2" /><ref>{{cite journal |last=Eliashberg |first=G. M. |year=1956 |title=О законе затухания для зонных моделей кристаллофосфоров |trans-title=On the Law of Decay for Band Models of Crystal Phosphors |journal=Оптика И Спектроскопия |language=ru |volume=1 |issue=2 |pages=230–239 |authorlink= |trans-journal=Optics and Spectroscopy}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last=Eliashberg |first=G. M. |year=1958 |title=Исследование начальных стадий нарастания свечения фосфора ZnS-Cu,Co |trans-title=Investigation of the Initial Stages of Luminescence Growth in the Phosphor ZnS-Cu,Co |journal=Оптика И Спектроскопия |language=ru |volume=4 |issue=1 |pages=66–75 |authorlink= |trans-journal=Optics and Spectroscopy}}</ref>

Following [[Stalin]]'s death in 1953 and the subsequent easing of restrictions, Eliashberg was admitted in 1959 to the [[Leningrad Physico-Technical Institute]] to begin doctoral studies in theoretical physics.<ref name=":0" /><ref name="q351" /> He became a junior research scientist there in 1961 and defended his candidate's dissertation in 1963. A year later he relocated to [[Chernogolovka]], a newly established science town about 50 kilometers outside Moscow. There he spent two years with the theoretical department of the [[Institute of Problems of Chemical Physics|Institute for Chemical Physics]]. In 1965 he joined the newly founded [[Landau Institute for Theoretical Physics|Institute of Theoretical Physics]] (later renamed the Landau Institute for Theoretical Physics) as a senior researcher, remaining there for the rest of his career.<ref name="q351" /> He earned his Doctor of Physical and Mathematical Sciences degree in 1972.<ref name="u973">{{cite journal |last1=Andreev |first1=A. F. |last2=Galitskii |first2=V. M. |last3=Ivlev |first3=B. I. |last4=Kolokolov |first4=I. V. |last5=Levitov |first5=L. S. |last6=Mineev |first6=V. P. |last7=Nazarov |first7=Y. V. |last8=Pitaevskii |first8=L. P. |last9=Pokrovskii |first9=V. L. |last10=Timofeev |first10=V. B. |last11=Khalatnikov |first11=I. M. |last12=Shibaeva |first12=R. P. |date=1 September 2020 |title=Gerasim Matveevich Eliashberg (on his 90th birthday) |url=https://ufn.ru/en/articles/2020/9/f/ |journal=Physics-Uspekhi |volume=63 |issue=9 |pages=940–941 |doi=10.3367/UFNe.2020.07.038809 |bibcode=2020PhyU...63..940A |issn=1063-7869 |access-date=6 October 2025|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

He died on 8 January 2021, in Chernogolovka, and was buried at the Makarovskoye Cemetery in the Moscow region.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.moscow-tombs.ru/2021/eliashberg_gm.htm |title=Eliashberg, Gerasim Matveyevich (1930–2021) |publisher=Moscow-tombs.ru |access-date=25 October 2021 |archive-date=25 October 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211025185243/http://www.moscow-tombs.ru/2021/eliashberg_gm.htm |url-status=live}}</ref>

He had two younger brothers, both of whom became scientists: electrical engineer Victor Eliashberg (born 1933) and mathematician [[Yakov Eliashberg]] (born 1946).<ref name=":0" />

== Scientific work ==
In March and November 1960, Eliashberg published two papers on [[superconductivity]]<ref>Russian original: {{cite journal |last=Элиашберг |first=Г.М. |year=1960 |title=Температурные функции Грина электронов в сверхпроводнике |trans-title= |journal=Журнал Экспериментальной И Теоретической Физики |language= |volume=39 |issue=5 |pages=1437–1441}}

English translation: {{cite journal |last=Éliashberg |first=G. M. |year=1961 |title=Temperature Green's function for electrons in a superconductor |url=http://www.jetp.ac.ru/cgi-bin/e/index/e/12/5/p1000?a=list |journal=Soviet Physics JETP |volume=12 |issue=5 |pages=1000–1002 |authorlink= |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210114082245/http://www.jetp.ac.ru/cgi-bin/e/index/e/12/5/p1000?a=list |archive-date=14 January 2021}}</ref><ref>Russian original: {{cite journal |last=Элиашберг |first=Г.М. |year=1960 |title=Взаимодействие электронов с колебаниями решетки в сверхпроводнике |journal=Журнал Экспериментальной И Теоретической Физики |volume=38 |issue=3 |pages=966–976}}

English translation: {{cite journal |last=Éliashberg |first=G. M. |year=1960 |title=Interactions between electrons and lattice vibrations in a superconductor |url=http://www.jetp.ac.ru/cgi-bin/e/index/e/11/3/p696?a=list |journal=Soviet Physics JETP |volume=11 |issue=3 |pages=696–702 |authorlink= |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210112022907/http://www.jetp.ac.ru/cgi-bin/e/index/e/11/3/p696?a=list |archive-date=12 January 2021}}</ref> that became classics in the field.<ref name=":2" /> In these works, he developed what is now known as the [[Eliashberg theory]], a microscopic model of electron–phonon superconductivity that extended the [[BCS theory|Bardeen–Cooper–Schrieffer (BCS) theory]]. Building on [[Lev Gor'kov]]'s Green's function formalism and [[Arkady Migdal]]'s theory of electron–phonon interactions in the normal (non-superconducting) state, Eliashberg’s formulation provided a quantitative framework for strong-coupling superconductors.<ref name="u973" /> The work was immediately recognized as a major achievement, as it clarified the success and the limitations of the BCS model.<ref name="q351" /><ref name=":2" /> It also provided a quantitative explanation of the phonon-related features observed in the tunneling spectra of lead, mercury and other strongly coupled superconductors.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Giaever |first1=I. |last2=Hart |first2=H. R. |last3=Megerle |first3=K. |date=1 May 1962 |title=Tunneling into Superconductors at Temperatures below 1°K |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRev.126.941 |journal=Physical Review |language=en |volume=126 |issue=3 |pages=941–948 |doi=10.1103/PhysRev.126.941 |bibcode=1962PhRv..126..941G |issn=0031-899X|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Bardeen |first=John |date=1972 |title=Nobel Lecture: Electron-Phonon Interactions and Superconductivity |url=https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/1972/bardeen/lecture/ |access-date=2 October 2025 |website=NobelPrize.org |language=en-US}}</ref> Eliashberg theory and its extensions have since become a standard tool for quantitative analysis of superconductivity in real materials and remains central to modern superconductivity research.<ref name=":2">{{cite journal |last1=Andreev |first1=A. F. |last2=Bychkov |first2=Yu. A. |last3=Gor'kov |first3=L. P. |last4=Ivlev |first4=B. I. |last5=Iordanskiĭ |first5=S. V. |last6=Kopnin |first6=N. B. |last7=Levitov |first7=L. S. |last8=Mineev |first8=V. P. |last9=Perel' |first9=V. I. |last10=Pitaevskiĭ |first10=L. P. |author-link10=Lev Pitaevskii |last11=Pokrovskiĭ |first11=V. L. |last12=Rashba |first12=É. I. |last13=Khalatnikov |first13=I. M. |date=October 1990 |title=Gerasim Matveevich Eliashberg (on his sixtieth birthday) |url=https://ufn.ru/ufn90/ufn90_10/ufn9010i.pdf |journal=Usp. Fiz. Nauk |volume=160 |issue= 10|pages=197–199 |doi= 10.3367/UFNr.0160.199010m.0197|access-date=}}</ref><ref name="k248">{{cite book |last=Zangwill |first=Andrew |title=A mind over matter: Philip Anderson and the physics of the very many |date=2021 |publisher=Oxford university press |isbn=978-0-19-886910-8 |publication-place=Oxford, United Kingdom |pages=170–174}}</ref><ref name="u973" />

During his stay in the Leningrad Physico-Technical Institute, Eliashberg developed a method of analytical continuation that enables the calculation of frequency-dependent quantities with the [[Matsubara frequency|Matsubara Green's function]] technique.<ref name="u973" /> He also generalized [[Landau's Fermi-liquid theory]] to finite temperatures, explaining the absence of [[zero sound]] in liquid [[helium-3]] and predicting the conditions under which it could later be observed experimentally.<ref>Russian original: {{cite journal |last=Элиашберг |first=Г.М. |year=1962 |title=Микроскопичесrая теория затухания нулевого звука в ферми-жидкости |journal=Журнал Экспериментальной И Теоретической Физики |language=ru |volume=42 |issue=6 |pages=1658–1666}}

English translation: {{cite journal |last=Éliashberg |first=G. M. |year=1962 |title=A microscopic theory of the damping of zero sound in a Fermi liquid |journal=Soviet Physics JETP |volume=15 |issue=6 |pages=1151–1157 |authorlink=}}</ref><ref name=":2" />

At the Landau Institute, Eliashberg made major contributions to [[nonequilibrium superconductivity]], developing a microscopic kinetic theory of superconductors in external fields and predicting [[microwave-stimulated superconductivity]], the amplification of superconductivity in a high-frequency field. The effect was later confirmed experimentally. In late 1960s and early 1970s, together with Lev Gor'kov, he derived a time-dependent generalization of [[Ginzburg–Landau theory]].<ref name="u973" /> Also in collaboration with Lev Gor'kov, he formulated a theory describing an ensemble of small metallic particles, anticipating aspects of modern [[mesoscopic physics]]. He also investigated strongly interacting [[two-dimensional electron system]]s, spin and charge transport in materials without inversion symmetry, and other problems in condensed matter physics.<ref name=":2" />

Eliashberg authored around 70 scientific publications.<ref>{{cite web |title=Publications of G. M. Eliashberg |url=https://www.itp.ac.ru/ru/persons/eliashberg-gerasim-matveevich/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210112022907/https://www.itp.ac.ru/ru/persons/eliashberg-gerasim-matveevich/ |archive-date=12 January 2021 |access-date=10 January 2021 |website=Landau Institute for Theoretical Physics}}</ref> He taught at the [[Moscow Institute of Physics and Technology]] and supervised doctoral students there.<ref name="timofeev21">{{cite web |author=Vladislav Timofeev |date=12 January 2021 |title=Eliashberg – a distinguished scientist and teacher |url=https://elementy.ru/nauchno-populyarnaya_biblioteka/435715/Svetlaya_pamyat_akademiku_Gerasimu_Eliashbergu_vydayushchemusya_uchenomu_i_pedagogu |access-date=30 March 2025 |website=elementy.ru |language=ru |quote=Original title: Элиашбергу — выдающемуся ученому и педагогу, published in: «Троицкий вариант — Наука» №1(320)}}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
Eliashberg's contributions were recognized both nationally and internationally.<ref name="u973" /> In 1970 he received the [[Jubilee Medal "In Commemoration of the 100th Anniversary of the Birth of Vladimir Ilyich Lenin"|Lenin centenary medal]]. He was elected a corresponding member of the [[Russian Academy of Sciences]] in 1990, and became a full member in 2000.<ref name="u973" /> In 1994 he was awarded, together with [[Anthony Leggett]], the John Bardeen Prize for his work on pairing theory in strongly coupled superconductors.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |title=Bardeen Prize |url=https://physics.illinois.edu/people/honors-and-awards/bardeen-prize |access-date=2 October 2025 |website=University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign |language=en}}</ref> In 2006, Eliashberg received the [[Order of Honour of the Russian Federation]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Элиашберг, Герасим Матвеевич |url=https://old.bigenc.ru/physics/text/5881038 |access-date=2 October 2025 |website=Большая российская энциклопедия 2004–2017 [The Great Russian Encyclopedia 2004–2017] |language=ru}}</ref>
